source.title: Midbrain-Hippocampus Structural Connectivity Selectively Predicts Motivated Memory Encoding.

confidence_rationale: Human diffusion-MRI/tractography study tying SN/VTA-hippocampus pathway density to VALUE-MODULATED (motivated) memory encoding -- the closest entry to MECH-189's actual target (a value/goal memory write), as opposed to generic episodic novelty. Two findings carry the verdict: (1) both reward AND punishment enhanced source memory equally (absolute salience, valence-symmetric), and (2) the paper explicitly frames the competing accounts -- SN/VTA-NAc reward-prediction-error vs SN/VTA-hippocampus signals -- as the open question, which is precisely DEV-NEED-024's adjudication axis. Supports an external value-PE-driven gate and confirms salience and complexity ride a shared dopaminergic channel. | 2026-06-24 tag-join: DEV-NEED-006 (the developmental WRITE-gate sub-need of MECH-189 -- high-salience benefit contact written to a durable super-ordinal goal anchor) added to claim_ids_tested. This paper evidences that WRITE gate as faithfully as it does MECH-189; the addition joins existing prior art to the DEV-NEED-006 experiment tag (v3_exq_588e) and clears a false novel_discovery quadrant flag that arose only because the experiment was tagged to the gate id while the literature was tagged to the parent claim.
failure_signatures: If the write gate is driven by a stimulus-novelty term divorced from value, it will miss value-modulated encoding: in humans, the strongest individual-difference predictor of motivated memory was SN/VTA-hippocampus tract density, a value pathway, not a generic novelty pathway.

Modelling gate (a) salience and gate (b) complexity as independent factors is at odds with the shared dopaminergic value/PE channel implicated here, where motivational value itself modulates the hippocampal encoding signal.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In humans, diffusion-weighted MRI tractography showed that SN/VTA-hippocampus (but not SN/VTA-striatum) pathway density was positively correlated with reward- and punishment-modulated source memory. Both reward and punishment enhanced source memory over neutral; the authors frame the mechanism as a competition between SN/VTA-NAc reward-prediction-error signals and SN/VTA-hippocampus signals underlying motivated memory encoding.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-189 writes a VALUE/goal anchor, not a neutral episodic trace, so the relevant biological gate is the motivated-memory / value-modulated encoding pathway -- which is dopaminergic and value-PE-linked. This supports super_ordinal_complexity_mode='external' driven by a value/prediction-error signal, and supports the salience gate being valence-symmetric (absolute benefit/harm magnitude, not signed valence).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Structural connectivity is a between-subject individual-difference correlate, not a within-trial causal demonstration of the write signal; the study measures source memory for words under monetary incentive, not a cross-episode super-ordinal goal store. The reward-PE-vs-hippocampal-novelty competition is presented as unresolved here, so the paper licenses 'value-PE matters' more than it adjudicates PE-vs-novelty cleanly.
mapping.source_context: Human adults; monetary-incentive source-memory paradigm; diffusion MRI + probabilistic tractography.

confidence_components.notes: Strong human data with a value/goal-memory target that maps unusually well onto MECH-189. Mapping fidelity good but capped because structural-connectivity correlates are indirect for a within-trial write signal. Transfer risk relatively low: human, value-modulated, declarative-to-goal extrapolation is modest.
